AR|Arkadelphia.intro: Arkadelphia is a college town of about 10,400 people and the county seat of Clark County. It sits at the foothills of the Ouachita Mountains on Interstate 30 between Little Rock and Texarkana.
family: Henderson State University and Ouachita Baptist University are both in the city.
The Arkadelphia Arts Center hosts exhibits, productions and educational workshops.
The Reynolds Science Center Planetarium is on the Henderson State campus.
outdoors: DeGray Lake, on the Caddo River, has 208 miles of shoreline and 13,800 acres of water.
DeGray Lake Resort State Park offers fishing, swimming, boating, hiking, horseback riding and an 18-hole golf course.
Hot Springs National Park, under an hour away, has hiking trails and camping areas.
sports: Henderson State's Reddies compete in NCAA Division II in the Great American Conference.
Henderson State and Ouachita Baptist share the longest rivalry in Division II football, the Battle of the Ravine, which began in 1895.
AR|Arkadelphia.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Arkadelphia far below the US average, with groceries, utilities and other everyday costs somewhat below it.
AR|Arkadelphia.climate: Summers are hot and humid and winters are generally mild to cool. Typical daily highs are about 55°F in January and about 94°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Hot Springs, under an hour away.
The main VA medical center for central Arkansas is in Little Rock, about an hour and 15 minutes away.
around: Interstate 30 runs through town.
Hot Springs is under an hour away by car and Little Rock about an hour and 15 minutes.
Texarkana is about an hour and a half away.

AL|Semmes.intro: Semmes is a small city of about 5,000 people in western Mobile County, part of the Mobile metropolitan area. It became a city in 2011.
family: Semmes School, a restored 1902 one-room school, is listed as an Alabama historical landmark.
The battleship USS Alabama, commissioned in 1942, is a museum ship docked in Mobile.
Mobile is known for Mardi Gras, the oldest organized Carnival celebration in the United States.
outdoors: Dauphin Island, a barrier island town in Mobile County, has beaches, popular fishing waters and the Dauphin Island Sea Lab.
Gulf State Park covers a large part of Gulf Shores, a Gulf of Mexico resort city about an hour and 45 minutes away.
sports: The University of South Alabama Jaguars play in the Sun Belt Conference and field 17 varsity sports.
The Senior Bowl, a college football all-star game, is played in Mobile each year in late January or early February.
AL|Semmes.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Semmes well below the US average, with groceries and utilities close to average.
AL|Semmes.climate: Semmes has a subtropical climate with mild, wet winters and very hot, humid summers, and the area can see hurricanes. Typical highs are about 60°F in January and about 91°F in July and August.
around: Downtown Mobile is about half an hour away by car.
U.S. Route 98, also called Moffett Road, is the main highway through Semmes and leads southeast into Mobile.

AL|Evergreen.intro: Evergreen is a small city of about 3,500 people and the county seat of Conecuh County in south Alabama. Interstate 65 passes the edge of town, about 75 miles from Montgomery and 90 miles from Mobile.
family: The town holds an annual Collard Green Festival, a nod to its 1973 designation as the collard green capital of Alabama.
Monroeville, about 45 minutes away, is known as the Literary Capital of Alabama and is the hometown of Harper Lee.
The battleship USS Alabama is a museum ship in Mobile, a little under two hours away.
outdoors: Conecuh National Forest covers about 83,000 acres in neighboring Covington and Escambia counties.
Open Pond Recreation Area in the forest offers hiking, fishing, bicycling and camping around a sinkhole lake.
The 20-mile Conecuh Trail runs through longleaf pine stands and hardwood bottomlands.
sports: The Montgomery Biscuits play Double-A baseball in Montgomery, about an hour and 40 minutes away.
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos play Double-A baseball in Pensacola, Florida, about two hours away.
AL|Evergreen.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Evergreen well below the US average, with groceries slightly below and utilities slightly above.
AL|Evergreen.climate: Summers are hot, with typical daily highs of about 91°F in July. Winters are mild, with typical highs of about 59°F in January.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Monroeville, about 45 minutes away.
The main VA location for central Alabama is in Montgomery, about an hour and 40 minutes away.
around: Interstate 65 runs northeast to Montgomery and southwest to Mobile.
Montgomery is about an hour and 40 minutes away by car and Mobile a little under two hours.
Pensacola, Florida, is about two hours away.

AZ|Goodyear.intro: Goodyear is a suburb west of Phoenix in Maricopa County, with about 118,000 residents. It began as cotton farmland bought by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company.
family: The city hall complex includes a public library and a two-acre park.
The White Tank Library and Nature Center offers nature programs for children, families and adults.
Franklin Pierce University has had a campus in Goodyear since 2008.
outdoors: Estrella Mountain Regional Park covers almost 20,000 acres of mostly desert, with more than 30 miles of trails.
White Tank Mountain Regional Park covers nearly 29,300 acres of desert and mountain, with almost 26 miles of hiking trails.
The Gila River passes through the city.
sports: Goodyear Ballpark hosts spring training for the Cleveland Guardians and Cincinnati Reds.
Phoenix Raceway in neighboring Avondale hosts two NASCAR race weekends a year.
AZ|Goodyear.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Goodyear well above the US average, with groceries, utilities and other everyday costs close to average.
AZ|Goodyear.climate: Goodyear has a hot desert climate with more than 300 sunny days a year. Winters are mild, with typical highs around 65°F in January, and summers are very hot, with July highs averaging about 105°F.
vets: The Phoenix VA medical center is in Phoenix, about half an hour away.
The VA also lists clinics in Surprise and in southwest Phoenix.
Luke Air Force Base is in the Glendale area, about half an hour away.
around: Phoenix is about half an hour away by car.
Glendale is also about half an hour away.
Tucson is about two and a half hours away.

AZ|Parker.intro: Parker is a town of about 3,400 people on the Colorado River and the county seat of La Paz County. It is also the headquarters of the Colorado River Indian Tribes.
family: The Colorado River Indian Tribes museum in Parker displays historical and contemporary artwork, especially ceramics, made by tribal citizens.
The Old Parker Jail, built in 1914, stands in a city park and is on the National Register of Historic Places.
Lake Havasu City, about 45 minutes away, is home to London Bridge.
outdoors: Buckskin Mountain State Park, near Parker, has Colorado River shoreline, camping and water recreation.
Parker Dam on the Colorado River creates Lake Havasu.
Blythe, California, a little over an hour away, has parks and boat ramps onto the Colorado River.
AZ|Parker.cost: BestPlaces index figures put groceries and housing in Parker a little below the US average, with utilities slightly above.
AZ|Parker.climate: Parker has an arid climate with very little rain, warm winters and extremely hot summers. Typical daily highs run from about 69°F in January to about 108°F in July.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Lake Havasu City, about 45 minutes away.
Another VA clinic is in Kingman, about two hours away.
around: Lake Havasu City is about 45 minutes away by car.
Quartzsite, about 40 minutes away, hosts major gem and mineral shows, mostly in January and February.
Phoenix is about three hours away.

AZ|Prescott.intro: Prescott is a city of about 46,000 people and the county seat of Yavapai County, known for its historic downtown and Whiskey Row. It was once the capital of the Arizona Territory and is home to several colleges, including Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's Prescott campus.
family: The Sharlot Hall Museum houses much of Prescott's territorial history.
The Heritage Park Zoo is in Prescott.
The courthouse plaza, a lawn under large old elm trees, hosts cultural events and performances on many summer nights.
outdoors: The Granite Dells, just north of the city center, are granite boulder formations with hiking trails that connect to the Peavine Trail.
Lynx Lake, set among tall ponderosa pines, offers boating, camping, fishing, hiking and mountain biking.
Goldwater Lake is a popular park with picnic facilities.
sports: Frontier Days, which bills itself as the World's Oldest Rodeo, has run every year since 1888 in the days leading up to July 4.
Four golf courses lie within the city limits, and two of them are city courses.
AZ|Prescott.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Prescott far above the US average, with groceries and utilities close to average.
AZ|Prescott.climate: Typical daily highs are about 53°F in January and about 90°F in July. A summer monsoon season brings rain and thunderstorms, and winter snowfall is typically light.
vets: The Northern Arizona VA Health Care System has its main medical center in Prescott.
VA outpatient clinics are also in Cottonwood, Flagstaff and other northern Arizona communities.
around: Prescott Regional Airport, about 7 miles north of the courthouse, has commercial service.
State Route 89A connects Prescott with Cottonwood and Sedona.
State Route 69 leads east to neighboring Prescott Valley.

AZ|Florence.intro: Florence is a town of about 27,000 people and the county seat of Pinal County. It sits on the south bank of the Gila River in the Sonoran Desert, between Phoenix and Tucson.
family: The historic downtown is a National Historic District with over 25 buildings on the National Register of Historic Places.
McFarland State Historic Park holds the first Pinal County Courthouse, built in 1876.
Casa Grande Ruins National Monument in nearby Coolidge preserves Hohokam structures from about 1150 to 1450.
outdoors: Picacho Peak State Park, between Casa Grande and Tucson, is known for spring wildflowers and steep trails with cables and catwalks.
The Superstition Mountains, east of the Phoenix area, have many hiking trails and include Lost Dutchman State Park.
Boyce Thompson Arboretum, near Superior, has more than 2,600 species of arid land plants and a 1.5-mile loop trail.
sports: The Florence Jr. Parada is described as the oldest junior rodeo in the United States.
The Phoenix Suns play in the NBA and the Arizona Diamondbacks in Major League Baseball, both in Phoenix.
Central Arizona College, near Coolidge, fields junior college teams in NJCAA Division I.
AZ|Florence.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Florence about even with the US average, with groceries a little lower and utilities slightly higher.
AZ|Florence.climate: Florence has a hot desert climate with mild winters and hot summers. Typical daily highs are about 66°F in January and about 102°F in July, and much of the summer rain comes with the monsoon from July through September.
vets: The VA lists clinics in Casa Grande.
The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for southern Arizona.
around: Phoenix and Tucson are each roughly an hour to an hour and a half away by car.
Casa Grande and Mesa are each about an hour away.

AZ|Payson.intro: Payson is a mountain town of about 16,000 people in northern Gila County, at about 5,000 feet of elevation. It sits within the Tonto National Forest below the Mogollon Rim.
family: Green Valley Park and Rumsey Park are the town's main parks, and there is a small skate park.
Green Valley Park has a replica of the cabin of author Zane Grey, who wrote about the area.
The August Doin's Rodeo has been held every year since 1884 and is called the world's oldest continuous rodeo.
outdoors: The town is surrounded by the Tonto National Forest.
Tonto Natural Bridge State Park, just northwest of Payson, holds what is described as the largest known natural bridge in the world.
Cold water lakes on top of the Mogollon Rim, north of Payson, are stocked with fish.
sports: The Phoenix Suns play in the NBA and the Arizona Diamondbacks in Major League Baseball, both in Phoenix.
AZ|Payson.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Payson somewhat above the US average, with groceries slightly below.
AZ|Payson.climate: Winters are mild with cold nights, with typical daily highs of about 56°F in January. Summer highs reach about 93°F in July, and monsoon thunderstorms from July through September bring a large share of the year's rain.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Payson, part of the Phoenix VA system.
The same system has clinics in Show Low and Globe, and its main medical center is in Phoenix.
around: State Route 87, the Beeline Highway, leads to the Phoenix area, roughly an hour and a half to two hours away by car.
State Route 260 leads east to Show Low, roughly two hours away.

AZ|Phoenix.intro: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona and its largest city, with about 1.6 million residents. It sits in the Salt River Valley in the Sonoran Desert.
family: The Phoenix Zoo in the Papago Park area has a children's trail with a petting zoo.
ZooLights, a December lighting show at the zoo, has run every year since 1991.
The Heard Museum, founded in 1929, is dedicated to American Indian art.
outdoors: South Mountain Park and Preserve has 58 miles of trails for hiking, cycling and horseback riding.
Camelback Mountain, North Mountain and Piestewa Peak rise within the heart of the valley.
The Desert Botanical Garden in Papago Park has more than 50,000 plants.
sports: The Arizona Diamondbacks, Phoenix Suns, Arizona Cardinals and Phoenix Mercury play in MLB, the NBA, the NFL and the WNBA.
The Phoenix area hosts the 15 major league teams of the Cactus League for spring training.
AZ|Phoenix.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Phoenix well above the US average, with groceries slightly below average and utilities close to it.
AZ|Phoenix.climate: Summers are long and extremely hot and winters are short and mild, with typical daily highs from about 68°F in January to about 107°F in July. Rain is scarce, and a summer monsoon season brings humidity and heavy, localized storms.
vets: The Phoenix VA medical center is in the city, with VA clinics in Mesa, Scottsdale, Gilbert, Surprise and other valley cities.
An Arizona Air National Guard air refueling wing is based at Phoenix Sky Harbor.
around: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, Arizona's largest and busiest, is about 3 miles east of downtown.
Tucson is roughly two hours away by car.
Flagstaff is roughly two and a half hours away.

AZ|Fort Mohave.intro: Fort Mohave is a community of about 16,000 people in western Mohave County, along the Colorado River just south of Bullhead City.
family: The Colorado River Museum in Bullhead City has replicas of area landmarks, Native American artifacts and historical displays.
Fort Mohave has a Mohave County Library branch.
Rotary Park in Bullhead City covers 300 acres of riverfront with beaches, a fishing jetty and boat launch ramps.
outdoors: Lake Mohave, a Colorado River reservoir near Bullhead City, is popular for swimming, kayaking, fishing, boating and water skiing.
Havasu National Wildlife Refuge protects 30 river miles of the lower Colorado River between Needles, California, and Lake Havasu City.
sports: Bullhead City hosts a youth soccer tournament at Rotary Park every February.
Bullhead City also sponsors senior softball tournaments each spring and fall.
AZ|Fort Mohave.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Fort Mohave below the US average, with groceries and utilities a little below it.
AZ|Fort Mohave.climate: The area has a desert climate with mild winters and very hot summers. In neighboring Bullhead City, typical highs are about 65°F in January and about 111°F in July.
vets: The VA lists clinics in Kingman and in Lake Havasu City.
around: Needles, California, is about half an hour away by car.
Lake Havasu City, home to London Bridge, is roughly an hour and 20 minutes away.
Las Vegas and its international airport are a little over two hours away.

AZ|Show Low.intro: Show Low is a city of about 12,000 people in Navajo County, on the Mogollon Rim in east central Arizona.
family: Northland Pioneer College has its White Mountain Campus in Show Low.
A city-run bus links Show Low with Pinetop-Lakeside, Taylor, Snowflake and Holbrook.
outdoors: The city is surrounded by extensive forests and is a popular recreation area.
The Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests cover about 2.76 million acres along the Mogollon Rim and the White Mountains.
Petrified Forest National Park is 28 miles east of Holbrook, which is roughly an hour from Show Low.
AZ|Show Low.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Show Low above the US average, with groceries below it.
AZ|Show Low.climate: Winters are cold, with typical daily highs around 46°F in January, and summers are warm, with highs around 85°F in July. Rain peaks in summer with the monsoon.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Show Low, part of the Phoenix VA system.
The system's main medical center is in Phoenix.
around: Pinetop-Lakeside is the neighboring town, roughly 20 minutes away by car.
Holbrook is roughly an hour away and Payson roughly two hours.
Phoenix is roughly three and a half hours away.

AZ|Yuma.intro: Yuma is a city of about 96,000 people on the Colorado River in the southwest corner of Arizona. It is the county seat of Yuma County.
family: Yuma Territorial Prison, which operated from 1876 to 1909, is now a historic park and museum.
Colorado River State Historic Park, on the site of a former army supply depot, has exhibits on the river and its steamboat era.
outdoors: The Colorado River runs along the north and west sides of town.
The Kofa mountain range and wildlife refuge are nearby, along with Martinez and Mittry lakes.
The Algodones Dunes, a few miles west of Yuma, are a large dune field where off-road riding is allowed in parts.
food: Yuma County supplies a large share of the nation's leafy vegetables from November to March, and the city is known as the Winter Lettuce Capital of the World.
The area grows more than 175 types of crops.
sports: The Yuma Jaycees Silver Spur Rodeo is held every February and opens with a parade.
AZ|Yuma.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Yuma well below the US average, with groceries slightly below and utilities slightly above.
AZ|Yuma.climate: Yuma has a hot desert climate with mild, dry winters and extremely hot summers. Typical highs are about 70°F in January and about 108°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Yuma, and the main VA medical center for southern Arizona is in Tucson.
Yuma is home to Marine Corps Air Station Yuma, and the Army's Yuma Proving Ground is in the area.
around: Yuma International Airport is the city's airport, and Interstate 8 runs west to San Diego.
El Centro, California, is roughly an hour away by car.
San Diego and Phoenix are each roughly three hours away.

AZ|Rio Rico.intro: Rio Rico is a community of more than 20,000 people in Santa Cruz County, just north of Nogales in southern Arizona.
family: Tumacácori National Historical Park protects the ruins of three Spanish mission communities and a 1937 museum building.
Tubac, an artists' colony on the Santa Cruz River, is roughly 25 minutes away.
Reid Park, Tucson's largest park, includes the Reid Park Zoo.
outdoors: Rio Rico sits where Sonoita Creek meets the Santa Cruz River.
Patagonia Lake State Park is a few miles from the town of Patagonia, which is roughly 45 minutes away.
food: Tucson was the first American city named a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, in 2015.
The Sonoita-Elgin wine country is about 20 miles east of Nogales.
AZ|Rio Rico.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and groceries in Rio Rico below the US average, with utilities slightly above.
AZ|Rio Rico.climate: In neighboring Nogales, typical daily highs run from about 66°F in January to about 97°F in June. The summer monsoon generally runs through July and August and brings much of the year's rain.
vets: The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for southern Arizona.
VA clinics are also listed in Green Valley and Sierra Vista.
around: Nogales, the county seat, is roughly 20 minutes away by car.
Tucson, the largest city in southern Arizona, is a little over an hour away.

AZ|Williams.intro: Williams is a small city of about 3,200 people in Coconino County, known as the Gateway to the Grand Canyon. It sits on Historic Route 66 and Interstate 40, about 42 miles west of Flagstaff.
family: The historic downtown covers six blocks, and Williams was the last town on Route 66 to be bypassed by Interstate 40.
Buckskinner Park has basketball and volleyball courts and a regularly stocked fishing lake.
Cataract Lake County Park has a stocked lake, barbecue areas and a playground.
outdoors: Bill Williams Mountain rises to 9,256 feet just south of town.
The Kaibab National Forest, about 1.6 million acres, is headquartered in Williams.
Grand Canyon Village on the South Rim, the park's main visitor area, is roughly an hour to an hour and a half away.
sports: The Northern Arizona University Lumberjacks compete in NCAA Division I, mostly in the Big Sky Conference, in Flagstaff.
The Arizona Snowbowl ski area is near Flagstaff.
AZ|Williams.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Williams above the US average, with groceries and utilities slightly below it.
AZ|Williams.climate: Williams has a cooler, wetter climate than most of Arizona. Typical daily highs are around 47°F in January and 84°F in July, and August is the wettest month.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Flagstaff.
The main VA medical center for northern Arizona is in Prescott.
around: Flagstaff is roughly 40 minutes east on Interstate 40.
Sedona, known for its sandstone formations and hiking trails, is roughly an hour and a quarter away.
Kingman is roughly two hours west.

AZ|Quartzsite.intro: Quartzsite is a town of about 2,400 people in La Paz County, right on Interstate 10. Winter visitors in RVs are a big part of local life, and major gem and mineral shows are held there, mostly in January and February.
family: The Quartzsite Museum is housed in Tyson's Well Stage Station, built beginning in 1866.
The gem and mineral shows fill the town each January and February.
London Bridge in Lake Havasu City is roughly an hour and a half to two hours away.
outdoors: The Dome Rock Mountains overlook the town on the west.
The Arizona Peace Trail, an off-highway route, passes through Quartzsite.
Kofa National Wildlife Refuge, southeast of town, offers desert wildlife viewing, rock climbing and remote camping.
sports: The Yuma Jaycees Silver Spur Rodeo is held every February in Yuma.
AZ|Quartzsite.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Quartzsite far below the US average, with groceries below average and utilities slightly above.
AZ|Quartzsite.climate: Quartzsite has a hot desert climate, with mild to warm winters from November to March and very hot summers. Typical daily highs run about 67°F in January and about 109°F in July.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Yuma.
The main VA medical center for southern Arizona is in Tucson.
around: Blythe, California, on the Colorado River, is roughly half an hour away by car.
Parker, the county seat, is roughly 45 minutes away.
Yuma is roughly an hour and a half to two hours away.

AZ|Willcox.intro: Willcox is a city of about 3,200 people in Cochise County, in the Sulphur Springs Valley of southeastern Arizona. Agriculture, wine production and tourism are its main industries, and Interstate 10 runs just north of town.
family: Rex Allen Days, held since 1951 on the first weekend in October, includes a parade, rodeos and a car show.
Willcox West Fest, usually in April, features a rodeo and a chuck wagon cook-off.
A Christmas light parade and craft fair is held in December.
outdoors: Chiricahua National Monument, about 36 miles southeast, has hoodoos, balancing rocks and about 17 miles of trails.
Sandhill cranes winter in the area around the Willcox Playa, a dry lakebed five miles south of town.
Fort Bowie National Historic Site preserves a 19th-century Army outpost, reached by a 1.5-mile foot trail.
food: Willcox is the largest wine grape growing region in Arizona.
Wine country festivals in spring and fall, usually the third weekends of May and October, include live music and arts and crafts.
sports: The University of Arizona Wildcats, in Tucson, compete in the Big 12 Conference.
AZ|Willcox.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Willcox far below the US average, with groceries below average and utilities above.
AZ|Willcox.climate: Willcox has a semi-arid climate, and summer monsoon rains bring it more rainfall than Tucson or Phoenix. Typical daily highs are about 61°F in January and about 96°F in July.
vets: VA clinics are in Safford, roughly an hour away, and Sierra Vista.
The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for the region.
Fort Huachuca, a U.S. Army post, is at Sierra Vista.
around: Benson, about 35 miles west on Interstate 10, is the gateway to Kartchner Caverns State Park.
Tucson, with its international airport and the University of Arizona, is about 80 miles west on Interstate 10.

AZ|Tucson.intro: Tucson is a city of about 540,000 people in southern Arizona. It is the county seat of Pima County and the home of the University of Arizona.
family: Reid Park, the city's largest park, includes the Reid Park Zoo.
The Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, west of town, blends a zoo, an aquarium and a botanical garden on 98 acres.
The Pima Air and Space Museum has close to 400 aircraft on 80 acres of grounds.
outdoors: Saguaro National Park has two districts, about 10 miles west and east of Tucson, with 165 miles of trails.
The Catalina Highway climbs Mount Lemmon from east Tucson, where the summit can be 20 to 30 degrees cooler than the valley.
Rillito River Park has a multi-use path for biking and walking.
food: Tucson was named the first American UNESCO City of Gastronomy in 2015.
Mission Garden, west of downtown at the foot of Sentinel Peak, grows heritage crops and heirloom trees.
sports: The University of Arizona Wildcats compete in NCAA Division I in the Big 12 Conference.
Wildcats baseball has won four national championships, and men's basketball won the national title in 1997.
AZ|Tucson.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and groceries in Tucson a little below the US average, with utilities close to average.
AZ|Tucson.climate: Summers are very hot and winters are mild. At nearby Saguaro National Park, typical daily highs are around 101°F in June and July and in the mid to upper 60s from December through February.
vets: The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for southern Arizona.
VA clinics are also in Green Valley, Casa Grande and Sierra Vista.
around: Phoenix is about 116 miles away by interstate, roughly two hours by car.
Nogales, on the Mexican border, is roughly an hour and a quarter away.
Sierra Vista is roughly an hour and a half away.

CA|Big Bear.intro: Big Bear is a mountain community in the San Bernardino Mountains. The city of Big Bear Lake, with about 5,000 people, sits on the south shore of the lake it is named for, next to Big Bear City.
family: Big Bear Lake has held an Oktoberfest every year since 1970.
A branch of the San Bernardino County Library serves the community.
The Big Bear Solar Observatory sits on the lake.
outdoors: Big Bear Lake is a large recreational lake with trout, bass and catfish.
San Bernardino National Forest surrounds the area and has many trails of varying difficulty.
The Pacific Crest Trail passes by Big Bear City.
sports: Snow Summit and Bear Mountain are the two ski resorts in the area.
The first Winter X Games were held in Big Bear Lake in 1997.
CA|Big Bear.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Big Bear Lake well above the US average, with groceries close to average and utilities somewhat above.
CA|Big Bear.climate: Winters are cold and bring significant snow, averaging close to 59 inches a season at lake level. Typical daily highs run about 46°F in January and about 80°F in July.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda.
VA clinics are also in Redlands, Rancho Cucamonga and Victorville.
around: San Bernardino is about 25 miles away, roughly an hour or more by mountain highway.
Redlands is roughly an hour away by State Route 38.
Ontario International Airport, the closest major airport, is roughly an hour and a half away.

CA|Merced.intro: Merced is a city of about 86,000 people and the county seat of Merced County in the San Joaquin Valley. It is known as the Gateway to Yosemite and is home to the University of California, Merced.
family: Castle Air Museum in Atwater, about 8 miles away, has more than 80 historical aircraft on 35 acres.
Lake Yosemite has shaded picnic areas with tables, barbecue pits and a small playground.
The County Courthouse Museum is one of the city's historic attractions.
outdoors: Lake Yosemite, about 5 miles east of Merced, allows boating and hosts sailing races on summer evenings.
Merced National Wildlife Refuge has wetlands and grasslands with large wintering flocks of sandhill cranes and geese.
Yosemite National Park is less than two hours away by car.
sports: UC Merced's teams compete in the California Pacific Conference in sports including soccer, water polo and basketball.
CA|Merced.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Merced above the US average, with groceries just below it.
CA|Merced.climate: Summers are hot and dry and winters are mild and damp. Typical daily highs run from about 56°F in January to about 96°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Merced.
The main VA medical center for central California is in Fresno.
around: Modesto is about 40 miles north, roughly an hour by car.
Fresno, 55 miles away, is a little over an hour by car.
Turlock is roughly half an hour north on State Route 99.

CA|Barstow.intro: Barstow is a city of about 25,000 people in the Mojave Desert of San Bernardino County, where Interstates 15 and 40 meet.
family: The Route 66 Mother Road Museum and the Western America Railroad Museum are housed in a 1911 Harvey House hotel and train station.
The Desert Discovery Center houses the Old Woman meteorite, the largest meteorite found in California.
Calico Ghost Town, a restored silver mining town and county regional park, is a few miles from Barstow.
outdoors: Rainbow Basin, 8 miles north of Barstow, draws photographers, hikers and campers.
Coyote Dry Lake, a large dry lakebed, is 15 miles northeast of town.
Lava tubes around Pisgah Crater can be explored.
sports: Barstow Community College fields men's and women's basketball, baseball and softball teams.
The city runs adult basketball and softball leagues, and its sports park has lighted ball fields, soccer fields and volleyball courts.
CA|Barstow.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Barstow well below the US average and groceries a little below, with utilities and transportation above average.
CA|Barstow.climate: Barstow has an arid climate with four seasons, very hot summers and cold winter mornings. Typical daily highs run from about 59°F in January to about 102°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Victorville, and the VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda.
Marine Corps Logistics Base Barstow is in the city, and the Army's National Training Center at Fort Irwin is north of town.
around: Victorville is about 32 miles south, roughly 40 minutes by car.
Los Angeles is roughly two hours away.
Las Vegas is roughly two and a half to three hours away.

CA|Blythe.intro: Blythe is a city of about 18,000 people in eastern Riverside County, in the Palo Verde Valley along the Colorado River. Interstate 10 crosses the city from east to west.
family: The city has six parks and a recreation center.
Palo Verde College, a public community college, is in Blythe.
The city also has two museums.
outdoors: The area is popular with campers and hikers, with three boat ramps onto the Colorado River and seven campgrounds.
The Blythe Intaglios, giant ground figures, are north of town.
sports: The city has an 18-hole public golf course.
CA|Blythe.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Blythe well below the US average, with groceries slightly below and utilities somewhat above.
CA|Blythe.climate: Blythe has a hot desert climate with mild winters and extremely hot summers. Typical highs are about 68°F in January and about 109°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Blythe.
The VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda, with another clinic in Palm Desert.
around: Quartzsite, Arizona, known for its winter gem and mineral shows, is roughly half an hour away.
Parker, Arizona, on the Colorado River, is roughly an hour away.
Indio, in the Coachella Valley, is nearly 100 miles west on Interstate 10, and Phoenix is about 150 miles east.

CA|Fresno.intro: Fresno is a city of roughly 540,000 people in California's San Joaquin Valley. It is the county seat of Fresno County and the largest city in the Central Valley region.
family: The Fresno Chaffee Zoo, in Roeding Park, covers 39 acres and houses over 190 species.
Woodward Park has three children's playgrounds, a lake and a Japanese garden.
Forestiere Underground Gardens are a series of hand-built underground rooms and gardens dating from the early 1900s.
outdoors: Woodward Park sits on the San Joaquin River, with trails that link to the Lewis S. Eaton Trail.
Yosemite National Park is about 60 miles north of Fresno.
Sequoia National Park is about 75 miles southeast, and Kings Canyon National Park is about 60 miles east.
food: Fresno is surrounded by some of the country's most productive farmland.
The Tower District is a neighborhood known for community events, including an annual literary festival.
sports: The Fresno State Bulldogs compete in NCAA Division I and have won national championships in softball and baseball.
The Fresno Grizzlies play Single-A baseball at a downtown ballpark.
Woodward Park has hosted the state high school cross country championships since 1987.
CA|Fresno.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Fresno somewhat above the US average, with groceries about average.
CA|Fresno.climate: Fresno has a semi-arid climate with cool, mild winters and long, hot, dry summers. Typical daily highs run from about 55°F in December and January to about 98°F in July, and winter can bring tule fog.
vets: The main VA medical center for central California is in Fresno.
VA clinics are also in Merced, Oakhurst and Visalia.
Naval Air Station Lemoore is roughly 45 minutes away.
around: Visalia is roughly an hour away by car.
Oakhurst, on Highway 41 toward Yosemite, is roughly an hour away.
Merced is 55 miles away, a little over an hour by car.

CA|Borrego Springs.intro: Borrego Springs is a desert village of roughly 3,000 people in northeastern San Diego County, surrounded by Anza-Borrego Desert State Park. It was the first community in California named an International Dark Sky Community, and the town has no stoplights.
family: More than 130 large metal animal sculptures stand in the desert around town.
Julian, a mountain town under an hour away, has held an Apple Days festival since 1949 and has a pioneer museum.
The San Diego Zoo Safari Park is near Escondido, roughly an hour and a half to two hours away.
outdoors: Anza-Borrego Desert State Park surrounds the town and covers about 650,000 acres.
The park has about 110 miles of hiking trails and 12 wilderness areas.
Spring wildflower blooms are among the park's biggest attractions in wet years.
food: Julian is known for its apple pie, and apples remain a local crop.
sports: The San Diego Padres play Major League Baseball in downtown San Diego, roughly two hours away.
An aerobatic club holds competitions at the Borrego Valley Airport each April and October.
CA|Borrego Springs.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Borrego Springs below the US average, with groceries slightly above and utilities above.
CA|Borrego Springs.climate: Winters are mild, with typical daily highs near 70°F in January. Summers are very hot, with highs near 107°F in July.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in San Diego.
VA clinics are listed in Escondido, El Centro, Oceanside and Chula Vista.
around: Julian is under an hour away by car.
Palm Springs is just under two hours away.
San Diego and its international airport are roughly two hours away.

CA|Bakersfield.intro: Bakersfield is a city of about 400,000 people and the county seat of Kern County, at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley. It is the birthplace of the country music style known as the Bakersfield sound.
family: The Kern County Museum has regional artifacts and a hands-on children's discovery museum.
The Buena Vista Museum of Natural History has a collection of marine fossils from the region.
The Kern County Fair each September showcases local agriculture with a rodeo, concerts and a carnival.
outdoors: The Kern River Parkway Trail follows the river for hiking and biking.
Panorama Vista Preserve, a 930-acre wildlife refuge in northeast Bakersfield, has hiking trails and biking paths.
Lake Isabella, a Kern River reservoir 35 miles away, is popular with boaters, water skiers and anglers.
food: Basque cooking is a long-standing part of the city's food history.
The Kern County Basque Festival on Memorial Day weekend features food, music, dance and handball.
sports: The Bakersfield Condors play professional hockey in the American Hockey League.
The Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners compete in NCAA Division I in the Big West Conference.
CA|Bakersfield.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Bakersfield somewhat above the US average, with groceries about average.
CA|Bakersfield.climate: Bakersfield has a hot, dry climate with nearly rainless summers and mild winters with chilly nights. Typical daily highs are about 59°F in January and 98°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Bakersfield.
The main VA medical center for the region is in Los Angeles.
around: Tehachapi, 35 miles east-southeast, is about an hour away and sits near the Pacific Crest Trail.
Los Angeles is roughly two hours away by car.
State Route 99 runs through the city.

KS|Parsons.intro: Parsons is a small city of about 9,600 people in southeast Kansas, the largest in Labette County, where U.S. Routes 59 and 400 meet. It is home to Labette Community College.
family: Forest Park, the city's largest park, hosts the Katy Days festival each Memorial Day weekend and a summer concert series
Marvel Park hosts the Fourth of July fireworks
The city has a municipal swimming pool and an arts center in the former Carnegie library
outdoors: Big Hill Lake, a Corps of Engineers reservoir about half an hour away, has fishing, boating, camping and a 17-mile horse trail
Lake Parsons, about half an hour away, has fishing, camping, boating and a beach on about 1,000 acres of public land
Fall River State Park, about an hour and twenty minutes away, has hiking trails, camping and boating
food: Local dining runs from barbecue to classic diners
Pittsburg, about 50 minutes away, holds an art walk on Broadway several times a year and the Little Balkans Days festival every Labor Day weekend
sports: Labette Community College Cardinals teams compete in the Kansas Jayhawk Community College Conference
Marvel Park's 2,000-seat stadium hosts Parsons High School Vikings football and college baseball
KS|Parsons.climate: Four seasons. Average highs are about 90 in July and the low 40s in January, with about 43 inches of precipitation a year. May and June are the wettest months.
around: Joplin Regional Airport in Missouri, about an hour and 10 minutes away, has commercial flights
Pittsburg is about 50 minutes away and Joplin about an hour and 15 minutes
Tulsa is about two hours and 20 minutes away and Wichita about two and a half hours

AK|Soldotna.intro: Soldotna is a small city of about 4,300 people on the Kenai River in the middle of Alaska's Kenai Peninsula. It is the borough seat and the service and shopping hub for the central peninsula.
family: Soldotna Creek Park has river access, a community playground, picnic pavilions and an amphitheater
The visitor center at the Kenai River bridge has wildlife displays, with the Homestead Museum nearby
The Kenai Watershed Forum runs a summer camp for kids ages 6 to 12 from Soldotna Creek Park
outdoors: The Kenai River holds all five species of Pacific salmon, and the city has several public river-access parks
The 1.9-million-acre Kenai National Wildlife Refuge starts at the edge of town, with a visitor center on Ski Hill Road
Tsalteshi Trails has more than 25 kilometers of trails for cross-country skiing in winter and hiking and mountain biking in summer
sports: The Kenai River Brown Bears, a junior hockey team in the North American Hockey League, play at the Soldotna Regional Sports Complex
AK|Soldotna.cost: Overall cost of living is close to the U.S. average and below the Alaska average. Alaska has no state income tax, and residents who have lived in the state for a full calendar year receive the annual Permanent Fund dividend.
AK|Soldotna.climate: Summers are cool, with July highs in the mid 60s. Winters are long and snowy but not especially cold for the latitude, with January highs around 20.
vets: A VA outpatient clinic is in Kenai, about 20 minutes away
A Vet Center satellite office is in Soldotna
around: Kenai Municipal Airport, about 20 minutes away, has scheduled commercial flights
Homer is about an hour and 50 minutes south on the Sterling Highway
Anchorage is about three hours and 20 minutes by road

AR|Texarkana.intro: Texarkana is a twin city on the Arkansas and Texas state line, with about 29,000 people on the Arkansas side. The federal courthouse and post office downtown sits directly on the state line.
family: The courthouse and post office that straddles the state line is the city's best-known landmark
Millwood State Park has camping, hiking and bike trails and a marina with boat rentals
The area has three colleges, including Texas A&M University-Texarkana
outdoors: Wright Patman Lake, a Corps of Engineers reservoir southwest of town, has nine Corps parks for boating and fishing
Atlanta State Park sits on the south shore of Wright Patman Lake
Millwood Lake and its state park offer fishing, camping and trails
food: Shreveport, about 72 miles south, has held the Mudbug Madness crawfish festival since 1984
Dallas, about 180 miles southwest, is the nearest very large city for dining and nightlife
sports: Texas A&M University-Texarkana is the local four-year university
War Memorial Stadium in Little Rock, about 143 miles northeast, hosts an Arkansas Razorbacks football game each year
Little Rock also has Double-A baseball, the Arkansas Travelers
AR|Texarkana.cost: People whose permanent home is inside the Texarkana, Arkansas city limits are exempt from Arkansas individual income tax.
AR|Texarkana.climate: Summers are hot and humid, with highs in the low 90s in July and August. Winters are mild, with January highs in the mid 50s, and snow is rare.
vets: A VA outpatient clinic is in Texarkana, Arkansas
Overton Brooks VA Medical Center is in Shreveport, about 72 miles away
Red River Army Depot is about 18 miles west of town
around: Texarkana Regional Airport has regional jet service to Dallas/Fort Worth
Interstate 30 and Interstate 49 meet here, along with U.S. 59, 67, 71 and 82
Amtrak's daily Texas Eagle stops at Union Station on the state line, and the city has a local bus system

AZ|Bullhead City.intro: Bullhead City is a desert city of about 41,000 people on the Colorado River at the south end of Lake Mohave. Laughlin, Nevada is directly across the river.
family: Rotary Park, a 300-acre riverfront park, has beaches, a skate park, a dog park and a lighted sports complex
Ken Fovargue Park has a public pool with a water slide, a playground, ball fields and a bike trail
The Colorado River Museum, open September through May, covers regional history
outdoors: Lake Mohave is a 67-mile stretch of the Colorado River for swimming, boating, kayaking and fishing
Katherine Landing, the largest marina on Lake Mohave, has launch ramps and campgrounds inside Lake Mead National Recreation Area
Oatman, an old gold-mining town on Route 66 in the Black Mountains, is known for its wooden sidewalks and wild burros
food: Laughlin's casino resorts are just across the river
Las Vegas, the closest large city, is 97 miles away
sports: Rotary Park hosts a large youth soccer tournament every February
The city hosts senior softball tournaments each spring and fall
AZ|Bullhead City.cost: Overall cost of living is about the U.S. average and below the Arizona average, and housing costs are below the U.S. average.
AZ|Bullhead City.climate: Summers are very hot, with average highs of about 107 to 111 from June through August and heat waves above 120. Winters are mild and sunny, with highs in the mid 60s to about 70, and rain is light.
vets: VA outpatient clinics are in Kingman and Lake Havasu City
The VA Southern Nevada medical center is in the Las Vegas area
around: Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas is the nearest major airport, with shuttle companies serving Bullhead City
Kingman is 34 miles east
State Routes 95 and 68 connect to Interstate 40, and the city has a local bus system

AZ|Kingman.intro: Kingman is a city of about 33,000 people in northwestern Arizona and the seat of Mohave County. It calls itself the Heart of Historic Route 66 and sits where Interstate 40 and U.S. 93 meet.
family: The Arizona Route 66 Museum is in the historic Powerhouse building
The downtown train station, a Mission Revival building, houses a model-railroad museum
Hualapai Mountain Park has cabins, camping and picnic areas in the pines
outdoors: Hualapai Mountain Park has more than 10 miles of hiking trails
Hualapai Peak, at 8,417 feet, is the highest point in Mohave County
The 40,000-acre Wabayuma Peak Wilderness lies in the southern Hualapai Mountains
food: Laughlin, a Colorado River resort town, is about 34 miles away
Las Vegas, about 107 miles northwest on U.S. 93, has big-city dining, shows and nightlife
sports: Las Vegas has the Raiders, the Golden Knights, the Aces and Triple-A baseball
Las Vegas also hosts NASCAR races and a Formula One grand prix each year
AZ|Kingman.cost: Overall cost of living is about the U.S. average and below the Arizona average, and housing costs are well below the U.S. average.
AZ|Kingman.climate: At about 3,500 feet, Kingman is milder than Phoenix or the river cities. July highs are near 99 with cooler nights, and winters bring highs in the upper 50s, freezing nights and occasional snow.
vets: A VA clinic is in Kingman
The Northern Arizona VA medical center is in Prescott
around: Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, about 104 miles northwest, is the nearest major airport
Interstate 40 runs east to Flagstaff, about 147 miles
Amtrak's Southwest Chief stops daily downtown, and the city runs a local bus system

AZ|Mesa.intro: Mesa is a city of about 504,000 people in the East Valley of the Phoenix metropolitan area, in the Sonoran Desert.
family: Red Mountain Park covers more than 1,100 acres with a lake, playgrounds and sports courts
Museums include the Arizona Museum of Natural History, the Mesa Historical Museum and the i.d.e.a. Museum for kids
The Mesa Arts Center downtown is one of the city's main cultural attractions
outdoors: Lost Dutchman State Park, on the west side of Superstition Mountain, has hiking and mountain bike trails
Saguaro Lake, a Salt River reservoir off State Route 87, is popular for bass fishing and boating
Canyon Lake, up the Apache Trail, has boating, camping and hiking beside the Superstition Wilderness
food: The Mesa Arts Center and Mesa Amphitheater host concerts and shows
Mesa is part of the Phoenix metro area, with big-city dining and nightlife close by
sports: The Chicago Cubs hold spring training at Sloan Park
The Athletics hold spring training at Hohokam Stadium
Arizona State University has its Polytechnic campus in southeast Mesa
AZ|Mesa.cost: Overall cost of living is slightly above the U.S. average, with utilities running below average.
AZ|Mesa.climate: A hot desert climate. Summers are very hot, with July highs near 106, and winters are mild, with January highs in the upper 60s. Rain is about 11 inches a year.
vets: VA clinics are in Mesa and neighboring Gilbert
The Phoenix VA medical center is on Indian School Road in Phoenix
Luke Air Force Base is west of Phoenix
around: Mesa Gateway Airport is in southeast Mesa, with fewer flights than Phoenix Sky Harbor
Phoenix Sky Harbor, an American Airlines hub, is just east of downtown Phoenix
Valley Metro light rail runs along Main Street through west and central Mesa

CA|Imperial.intro: Imperial is a small city of about 20,000 people in California's Imperial Valley farming region, four miles north of El Centro.
family: The California Mid-Winter Fair runs for 10 days in Imperial each year around the end of February
Imperial Market Days is a free downtown event series that starts each October
El Centro's city parks include Bucklin Park, Countryside Park and Legacy Park
outdoors: The Imperial Sand Dunes Recreation Area, also called Glamis, is open to off-road vehicles and camping
The Salton Sea is a major stop for migrating birds on the Pacific Flyway
food: The valley's farms grow winter vegetables such as lettuce and carrots
The Mid-Winter Fairgrounds in Imperial hosts festivals, concerts and car races through the year
sports: Naval Air Facility El Centro is the winter training home of the Blue Angels, who traditionally open their season with an air show there
CA|Imperial.climate: A hot desert climate with long, extremely hot summers and mild winters. Highs are about 104 in July and August and in the upper 60s in December and January, with about 3 inches of rain a year.
vets: Naval Air Facility El Centro is a few miles away
A VA clinic serves the Imperial Valley in El Centro, and the VA medical center is in San Diego
around: Imperial County Airport is in Imperial, and the nearest large airport is San Diego
Interstate 8 runs west to San Diego, about 113 miles, and east to Yuma, Arizona
Imperial Valley Transit runs local buses

CA|San Bernardino.intro: San Bernardino is a city of about 222,000 people and the county seat of San Bernardino County, a regional hub of Southern California's Inland Empire at the foot of the San Bernardino Mountains.
family: Cal State San Bernardino has an accredited art museum and an observatory with public viewing nights
Lake Arrowhead Village holds events all year, including free summer concerts
The Western Regional Little League Championships are played in San Bernardino each August
outdoors: San Bernardino National Forest, more than 800,000 acres, is headquartered in the city
Big Bear Lake in the mountains has fishing, hiking and skiing at Snow Summit and Bear Mountain
The Rim of the World Highway climbs from the city past Lake Arrowhead to Big Bear Lake
food: Downtown hosts the Route 66 Rendezvous each September
Big Bear Lake has held an Oktoberfest every year since 1970
sports: The Inland Empire 66ers play minor league baseball at San Manuel Stadium
Cal State San Bernardino Coyotes teams compete in NCAA Division II
CA|San Bernardino.cost: Overall cost of living is above the U.S. average, mostly because of housing, but typical home costs are well below the California average.
CA|San Bernardino.climate: Summers are hot and dry, with July and August highs in the mid to upper 90s. Winters are mild, with highs in the upper 60s and chilly mornings, and about 16 inches of rain a year.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in neighboring Loma Linda
VA clinics are also in Redlands, Rancho Cucamonga, Victorville, Corona, Hemet and Palm Desert
March Air Reserve Base is near Riverside
around: Ontario International Airport is about 18 miles west of downtown, and San Bernardino International Airport has limited airline service
Metrolink trains run daily to Los Angeles Union Station
Interstates 10 and 215 and State Route 210 meet here

CO|Englewood.intro: Englewood is a city of about 34,000 people immediately south of Denver in the South Platte River valley, part of the Denver metropolitan area.
family: The Denver Museum of Nature and Science has a planetarium and a play area for young children
The Denver Zoo covers 80 acres in Denver's City Park
Englewood's Civic Center holds the public library and the Museum of Outdoor Arts
outdoors: The South Platte River trail runs through the city
Cherry Creek State Park has an 880-acre reservoir, a swim beach and about 35 miles of trails
Chatfield State Park centers on a 1,400-acre reservoir and is known for birdwatching
food: Downtown Denver and its historic LoDo district are a light rail ride away
Red Rocks Amphitheatre has hosted concerts since 1941
sports: Denver has the Broncos, Nuggets, Avalanche, Rockies and Rapids
The Broncos play at Empower Field at Mile High, and the Nuggets and Avalanche play at Ball Arena
CO|Englewood.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Englewood well above the US average, with groceries close to average and utilities a little below. Colorado has a flat state income tax.
CO|Englewood.climate: Four seasons in a dry climate. Highs are in the upper 80s in July and the low 40s in January.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Englewood itself
The region's main VA medical center is in Aurora, with more VA clinics in Golden and Castle Rock
Buckley Space Force Base is in nearby Aurora
around: Denver International Airport is a United Airlines hub
RTD light rail runs from Englewood station to downtown Denver
Interstate 25 is a few miles east

CO|Frisco.intro: Frisco is a mountain town of about 2,900 people in Summit County, Colorado, on the shore of Dillon Reservoir at about 9,000 feet. It is a base for skiers, with four major resorts close by.
family: Dillon Amphitheater, beside the Dillon marina, hosts concerts and community events through the summer
Breckenridge holds a Fourth of July parade and an international snow sculpture competition each January
Free Summit Stage buses run between Frisco, Silverthorne, Breckenridge and other towns
outdoors: Dillon Reservoir has an 18-mile paved path around its shore and is stocked with rainbow trout every year
Frisco and Dillon both have marinas on the reservoir, with sailing and boat rentals
Breckenridge, Copper Mountain, Keystone and Arapahoe Basin ski resorts are all close to town
food: Breckenridge's historic Main Street, about 20 minutes away, is lined with shops and restaurants
Denver, about an hour and a half away, has big-city dining, museums and a large performing arts complex
sports: Denver has the Broncos, Rockies, Nuggets, Avalanche and Rapids
Skiing and snowboarding are the local sports, with four resorts nearby
CO|Frisco.cost: Cost of living is well above both the U.S. and Colorado averages, driven mostly by very high housing costs.
CO|Frisco.climate: A high-mountain climate. Summer highs are in the low 70s, January highs are around 30, and snow generally falls from late September to mid-May.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in Aurora, on the east side of Denver
VA clinics are also in Englewood and Golden
around: Denver is about an hour and a half east on Interstate 70, and Denver International Airport is about two hours
Eagle County Regional Airport, about an hour and 15 minutes west, has seasonal flights
Bustang buses stop in Frisco between Denver and Grand Junction, and Summit Stage runs free local buses

FL|Venice.intro: Venice is a city of about 25,000 people on Florida's Gulf Coast in Sarasota County, part of the Sarasota metropolitan area.
family: Venice is known for the fossilized shark teeth found on its beaches and holds an annual Shark's Tooth Festival
Sarasota, about 35 minutes away, has the Ringling Museum of Art and the Mote Marine Laboratory aquarium
Siesta Beach near Sarasota is a year-round draw
outdoors: Venetian Waterway Park is a 9.3-mile paved trail along both sides of the Intracoastal Waterway
Myakka River State Park, about 30 minutes away, covers 37,000 acres with a canopy walkway, boardwalk and canoeing
Oscar Scherer State Park, about 15 minutes away, has swimming, scrub jay habitat and the Legacy Trail
food: Sarasota, about 35 minutes away, has an opera house, theaters and a performing arts hall
Tampa's historic Ybor City district is about an hour and 25 minutes away
sports: The Atlanta Braves hold spring training in North Port, about 30 minutes away
The Baltimore Orioles hold spring training at Ed Smith Stadium in Sarasota
Tampa, about an hour and 25 minutes away, has the Buccaneers, Lightning and Rays
FL|Venice.cost: Overall cost of living is a little above the U.S. and Florida averages, with housing somewhat above average. Florida has no state income tax.
FL|Venice.climate: Hot, humid summers with highs in the low 90s and mild winters with highs in the low to mid 70s. June through September are the wettest months, and the area can be affected by hurricanes.
vets: VA clinics are in Sarasota and Port Charlotte, part of the Bay Pines VA system
MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa is about an hour and 35 minutes away
around: Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport, just north of downtown Sarasota, has service from several airlines
Sarasota is about 35 minutes away and Tampa about an hour and 25 minutes
Interstate 75 and U.S. 41, the Tamiami Trail, run through the city

IA|Audubon.intro: Audubon is a small farm town of about 2,000 people and the county seat of Audubon County in western Iowa, roughly halfway between Des Moines and Omaha.
family: Albert the Bull, a 30-foot-tall, 45-ton statue, is the town's landmark
Omaha, about an hour and 35 minutes away, has the Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium and the Durham Museum
Des Moines, about an hour and 45 minutes away, has the Science Center of Iowa and a botanical garden
outdoors: Prairie Rose State Park near Harlan has a 218-acre lake and 7 miles of multi-use trails
Prairie Rose Lake has two boat ramps and fishing for bass, bluegill, catfish and crappie
food: Des Moines has touring Broadway shows and concerts at its Civic Center
Omaha is the other big city for dining and nightlife, about an hour and 35 minutes away
sports: The Iowa Cubs play minor league baseball in Des Moines
The College World Series is held in Omaha every year
IA|Audubon.cost: Cost of living is well below both the U.S. and Iowa averages, and housing costs are far below the national average.
IA|Audubon.climate: Four distinct seasons. July highs are in the low 80s and January highs are in the upper 20s, with about 24 inches of snow a year.
vets: The VA medical center for central Iowa is in Des Moines
A VA clinic is in Carroll
Offutt Air Force Base is just south of Omaha
around: Des Moines is about an hour and 45 minutes away and Omaha about an hour and 35 minutes
The nearest commercial airports are Des Moines International and Omaha's Eppley Airfield
U.S. Route 71 runs through town and meets Interstate 80 near Brayton

ID|Driggs.intro: Driggs is a small city of about 2,000 people and the seat of Teton County in eastern Idaho. It sits in the Teton Valley at about 6,100 feet, on the west side of the Teton Range.
family: Grand Teton National Park, just north of Jackson, Wyoming, covers about 310,000 acres including the Teton Range
The Idaho Falls Zoo, about an hour and 40 minutes away, has more than 300 animals
Jackson's town square, about an hour away, is surrounded by shops, restaurants and art galleries
outdoors: Grand Targhee Resort, about 12 miles away in Alta, Wyoming, averages more than 500 inches of snow a year
The resort sits in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest
The South Fork of the Snake River nearby is a well-known place to fish for wild trout
food: Jackson, about an hour away, has a dining and shopping district around its town square
Idaho Falls, about an hour and 40 minutes away, has a downtown with restaurants and a farmers market
sports: The Idaho Falls Chukars play Pioneer League baseball in Idaho Falls
Skiing and snowboarding at Grand Targhee are the local winter sports
ID|Driggs.cost: Cost of living is above both the U.S. and Idaho averages, mainly because of housing. Groceries and utilities run below the national average.
